reading.body:
EPAM Systems files as a computer programming services company on the NYSE, and the record shows no AI product, no data center, and no power position of its own.

The filings are routine: two 10-Qs, five 8-Ks, and one proxy statement between March and August 2026. That cadence is what a public operating company produces, not what a company building AI infrastructure produces. Nothing in the data names a model, a chip, a facility, or a megawatt.

For AI specifically, this matters as a boundary case. EPAM sells software engineering, design, and consulting services across 11 industries and 55 or more countries, according to its own site text. That is labor and expertise, not compute. A services firm can absorb AI into how it delivers work without ever appearing in the compute supply chain, and this record is consistent with that.

What the data does not tell the reader is anything about EPAM's actual AI revenue, its customer contracts, or whether it resells another company's AI capacity. No products, MCP servers, or lawsuits are recorded. The absence is a limit of the record, not a finding about the business.

profile_text.body:
EPAM Systems is a software engineering and product development services company that, in its own words, has helped customers digitally transform their businesses since 1993 through a blend of software engineering, design and consulting services. The company describes its teams as technologists, strategists and designers who deliver digital experiences, and says it specializes in 11 industries across 55+ countries and regions. Its site lists office addresses in Bengaluru, Karnataka and Gurugram, Haryana, India.

The material provided does not describe any specific AI products from the company. No products, MCP servers, or lawsuits are recorded for EPAM Systems.

EPAM Systems, Inc. is a public company traded under the ticker EPAM and registered with the SEC under CIK 0001352010.
